blocks: 1. Sign in to ShopView on a desktop computer with a mouse (hover actions do not appear on touch screens).
2. Have records across several types (work orders, customers, assets, parts, vendors, part sales, purchase orders) that match a common search term.

3. Optional: be part-way through editing a work order elsewhere in the app, so the actions that need a 'current work order' can be checked.

blocks: 1. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search.
2. Type a term that returns results across the entity types.
3. Move the mouse over each result row and read the action button(s) that appear on the right.
custom_steps.text:
1. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search.
2. Type a term that returns results across the entity types.
3. Move the mouse over each result row and read the action button(s) that appear on the right.

blocks: 1. On hover, a quick-action button appears on the right of the row for each entity that has one — shown unconditionally (there is no state that hides the action for an entity that has one).

2. The actions by entity are: Work Order → 'Add new line'; Customer → 'New work order' and 'New contact'; Asset → 'New work order' plus history and invoices icon buttons; Part → 'Add to work order' and 'View part history'; Vendor → 'Add contact'; Part Sale → 'Add part'; Purchase Order → 'Receive'; Vendor Invoice → none.
3. Actions that need a target work order ('Add new line', 'Add to work order') act on the work order the user is currently editing elsewhere in the app.
4. No quick action deletes or changes data destructively, and every action is also reachable from the entity's own record and by keyboard.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.3 (Confluence page 576978945), section 5.4 (quick actions), read on 2 September 2026.

Note: these quick actions were previously parked as out-of-v1. Spec v1.3 (2026-09-01, section 5.4) brings them back into v1 — shown unconditionally, with 'View part history' added to Part rows — and the design shows them; this is newer than the epic's out-of-scope note, so this case follows the current spec.
